Hi Sarah — really helpful set of questions. Attached is a short proposal (redwood-minimal-downtime-proposal.pdf) and an initial sprint-level timeline (initial-migration-sprint-plan.xlsx). High-level approach in summary: 

1) Pre-flight (2–3 weeks): schema mapping, production telemetry baseline, prefix/KV cache snapshot, small-scale replay testing against a staging shard.
2) Pilot canary (2–3 days): route 1–3% of traffic to a dedicated canary pool with KV-cache warmup and A/B scoring. Gate on latency P95, error rate, and business correctness checks.
3) Gradual ramp (4–7 days): phased traffic shifts by region and affinity buckets with automated KV-prefetch and progressive batch size increases to maintain token throughput.
4) Final cutover (2 business hours coordination window): lightweight DNS and routing updates with immediate rollback hooks. If a rollback is triggered, fallback to pinned model variant and session replay rehydration.

I'll call out specific gating thresholds in the attached PDF (e.g., P95 latency delta <= 12%, error rate delta <= 0.1%, model accuracy acceptance tests pass against the golden prompt set). Lauren will spell out operational gates and runbook steps for canary monitoring.

Questions for you: what blackout windows do you have for schema changes? And who will be the delegated runbook approver on your side during the final cutover?

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Hi Sarah — looping in operational details from enablement/CS side. Below are the concrete canary gates and the integration checklist we recommend including in the SOW.

Canary gates (must be green to advance):
- Traffic stability: rolling 30-minute window where P95 latency delta <= 12% and P99 delta <= 25% relative to baseline.
- Error budget: no more than 0.05% increase in 5xx errors for canary group.
- Functional correctness: pass rate >= 99% on a curated set of 250 golden prompts reflecting IvyBank flows.
- Cost/throughput: observed tokens/sec within 85–110% of predicted for canary pool.

Rollback triggers (any trigger causes immediate traffic reversion):
- Sustained P95 degradation > 20% for 30 minutes;
- New class of semantic regressions detected by automated evals;
- Unrecoverable KV-cache miss storms causing client errors.

Integration checklist (high level):
- Schema mapping file (sample attached: schema-mapping-sample.csv) and migration transform scripts committed to repo.
- Telemetry hooks: per-request tracing header (x-rdw-trace-id), token-level cost counters, and per-route latency tagging.
- Canary automation: CI job to provision canary pool and a runbook playbook in Confluence.
- Ops contact roster and 24x7 escalation path for final cutover.

We recommend a dry-run where we execute the full pilot sequence against a production-like snapshot during a low-traffic weekend to validate rollout automation. I'll sync with Aditya and Priyom to propose exact weekend dates in the timeline sheet.

—Lauren
Principal Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
